title: Gifter escrow: swap token A for token B, with a refund
summary: A maker opens an escrow PDA, deposits mint A into a vault the PDA owns, and names the mint B and amount they want. On the hosted program recorded 13 Nov 2026, a taker can pay that amount of mint B and receive the vault's mint A, and the maker can refund instead. An earlier devnet program's take aborted. That program is not the one this page hosts.
what: Gifter is a two-mint escrow. `create_escrow` initializes a **GifterEscrow** PDA at `["gifter_escrow", maker, escrow_id]` (the id is a `u64`, little-endian in the seeds, so one maker can have several escrows) and an associated token account for mint A whose authority is that PDA. The maker's mint A is deposited with `transfer_checked`. The maker can `refund`: the program signs as the PDA to send the vault's whole balance back, then closes the vault and the escrow (rent to the maker). `take_and_close` does the swap: the taker pays `maker_expected_price` of mint B, the PDA signs the vault's mint A to the taker, and both accounts close to the taker. On 13 Nov 2026 that completed on program `45C1bSkF…` ([33yMgZzA…](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/33yMgZzAaH3mMcHgSmQBRVb4FeRmu5gX6nkAMfJU2T8F8sAwqMDTVfgsVcg7MXPM28GoAo7RPC7E35NhkNSrLXZd?cluster=devnet)). An earlier program, `6Z5cvVUc…`, aborted take with an access violation ([ck53TqoU…](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/ck53TqoU8UfpBav2V3bE1oy4Wm2qvxeU6bgibkXqzCsbP4YbBxDGK98bJxoowGpKNwkkPotBtCxVfUQMEm2zZu7?cluster=devnet)). That record is the article [Why this escrow take failed](/articles/why-this-escrow-take-failed/).
app_note: The fork's own Next.js app (`gifter-escrow-frontend`) exported as static pages with this devnet program ID. Program transactions use the public devnet RPC (`clusterApiUrl('devnet')`). Token lists use Helius DAS via a build-time env URL in the hosted JS only (never in the source we cite, the recipe, or the logs). The committed `config` still has the author's program ID `9HP45DvS…`. The hosted build recorded on 13 Nov 2026 talks to `45C1bSkF…`. Script: [tests/devnet/gifter-escrow.mjs](https://github.com/Blockchains/sol-college/blob/main/tests/devnet/gifter-escrow.mjs).

try_steps.do: Open [the app](/dapps/gifter-escrow/) and connect a Phantom wallet on **devnet**.
try_steps.see: A Create Escrow heading. On the 13 Nov 2026 click-through the token dropdown listed 18 options after connect, including mint A and mint B. The escrow list is fetched once at connect and does not refresh until you reload.

try_steps.do: If an open escrow card is shown and you are not the maker, press **Accept**.
try_steps.see: Accept calls `take_and_close`. This click-through did not press Accept, because no escrow opened by someone else was left on the page. The script's take of escrow #1 completed: T paid 5 of mint B, received 10 of mint A, and the vault and state closed (33yMgZzA…). The card still promises a GFT reward the program does not mint.
try_steps.ran_note: Accept was not clicked in the UI. The completed take is the script transaction 33yMgZzA… in Proof. The earlier program's failing take is ck53TqoU….

try_steps.do: As the maker, press **Cancel** on your own card if one is open.
try_steps.see: That calls `refund`: the vault's mint A returns to the maker and both accounts close. On 13 Nov 2026 the click-through did this for escrows #535 and #772. An outsider cannot refund: the PDA is seeded by the signer, and that attempt returned **AccountNotInitialized**.
try_steps.ran_note: The 13 Nov click-through refunded escrow #535 (3GUdvNGQ…) and escrow #772 (2GsfGiPt…). The script refunded escrow #2 (3qwx8QBC…) after a take for more mint B than the taker held was rejected. An outsider refund still fails with AccountNotInitialized.

diagram:
maker ─ create_escrow(id, deposit, expected_price)
          ─▶ GifterEscrow PDA ["gifter_escrow", maker, escrow_id u64 LE]
          ─▶ Vault ATA (mint A, authority = PDA)   ← deposit of mint A (transfer_checked, maker signs)
maker ─ refund ─▶ Vault ──all mint A──▶ maker   (PDA signs); vault closed; escrow closed to maker
taker ─ take_and_close ─▶ (intended) taker ──expected_price of mint B──▶ maker
                          Vault ──all mint A──▶ taker   (PDA signs); vault closed; escrow closed to taker
                          RECORDED on 45C1bSkF…: take of escrow #1 completed (33yMgZzA…)
                          EARLIER program 6Z5cvVUc…: take aborted, access violation 0x10008 (ck53TqoU…)
accounts: `escrow_id`, `maker_expected_price`, `maker`, `mint_a`, `mint_b`, `deposit_amount`, `bump`. `INIT_SPACE` is 129 bytes (8-byte discriminator plus those fields).
ATA of mint A, authority = the GifterEscrow PDA
Holds the deposited mint A. It can only move tokens through a Token Program `transfer_checked` the program signs with the PDA's seeds.

instructions.name: `create_escrow`: a numbered PDA and a vault ATA
steps: Seeds are `["gifter_escrow", maker, escrow_id.to_le_bytes()]`, so the same maker and id can only exist once. Recreating escrow #1 failed with **Allocate: account … CzEL5a2v… already in use**.

The vault is `init`'d as the PDA's associated token account for mint A. `initialize_gifter_escrow` stores the two mints, the two amounts and the bump; `deposit_to_escrow_vault` then `transfer_checked`s `deposit_amount` of mint A from the maker, signed by the maker (an ordinary CPI, not PDA-signed).

Create does not check that a taker can pay. On the earlier program, escrow #2 asked for 10_000 of mint B and still created (4M4aWcN7…). The 13 Nov 2026 record did the same on `45C1bSkF…` (jJPixCQg…): the take was then rejected for insufficient funds, and the maker refunded.
The fork's `declare_id!` and `Anchor.toml` still say `9HP45DvS…`. The hosted program recorded on 13 Nov 2026 is `45C1bSkF…`. Local builds target the declared id unless you change it.

instructions.name: `refund`: the vault signs, only the maker, accounts close
steps: `Refund` derives the escrow from `["gifter_escrow", maker.key(), state.escrow_id.to_le_bytes()]` with `bump = state.bump` and `close = maker`. The signer *is* the seed, so an outsider's derivation misses: X refunding M's open escrow got **AccountNotInitialized**.

`withdraw_from_vault` builds signer seeds `["gifter_escrow", maker, escrow_id, bump]` and `transfer_checked`s `escrow_vault.amount` (the whole balance, not a stored number) back to the maker, then `close_account`s the vault to the maker. The escrow account itself is closed by the `close = maker` constraint.

On the earlier program, M refunded escrow #1 (5tpaLaSh…) after the take had aborted, so the 10 of mint A was still in the vault. On 13 Nov 2026 the script refunded escrow #2 (3qwx8QBC…) after the oversized take was rejected, and the click-through refunded two escrows from the form.

instructions.name: `take_and_close`: the swap, and the earlier abort
steps: The accounts are the two parties' ATAs for both mints (`init_if_needed` on the ones that might not exist, paid by the taker), the escrow (`close = taker`, same PDA seeds with the `maker` account and the stored id) and the vault. `send_to_maker` should `transfer_checked` `maker_expected_price` of mint B from the taker to the maker; `take_from_vault` should PDA-sign a transfer of the vault's mint A to the taker and close the vault to the taker.

**Earlier failure, program `6Z5cvVUc…`:** take of escrow #1 (ck53TqoU…) finalized as `ProgramFailedToComplete`. The log was `Instruction: TakeAndClose`, then an access violation reading 8 bytes at `0x10008`. The note written against that program attributed the abort to `println!("Hello")` at the start of `send_to_maker`. The opened pull request records a second cause after that line was removed: `to_le_bytes().as_ref()` inside the seeds attribute was a dangling pointer. **This hosted commit** (`fb2bbfd`, program `45C1bSkF…`) has no `println!` in `send_to_maker`. The PDA check uses owned seed bytes in the handler, and that handler still calls `create_program_address`. The recorded take on this program completed (33yMgZzA…).

The current `Take` accounts constrain `maker` to the stored key. The excerpt still does not constrain `mint_a` or `mint_b` to the stored mint keys. A take that substitutes a different mint B was not run. That is exercise 2, and it is still open.

innovation.title: an ATA vault the escrow PDA owns, and a swap that has to close cleanly
innovation.text: The escrow's state and its tokens are two accounts, as in Friendstake, but here the vault is an **associated token account** whose authority is the GifterEscrow PDA, not a system-owned lamport account. Every movement of mint A out of the vault is a Token Program `transfer_checked` signed with `["gifter_escrow", maker, escrow_id, bump]`. Refund shows that pattern, and so does the take recorded on 13 Nov 2026 (33yMgZzA…): mint B moves to the maker, mint A leaves the vault, and both accounts close. The earlier abort, on a program this page no longer hosts, is written up in [Why this escrow take failed](/articles/why-this-escrow-take-failed/).

refs.note: the PDA signs the refund and closes the vault
hosted commit: send_to_maker has no println!

more: Compare TrustLock, which escrows SOL in a program-owned account and uses Clock for a deadline. This program has no expiry: the deposit waits for a take or for the maker's refund.

On the earlier program, `println!("Hello")` was the first statement of `send_to_maker`. On BPF that is not `msg!`. The access violation at `0x10008` was recorded on that program (ck53TqoU…). It is not the behavior of the hosted program `45C1bSkF…`.

frontend.title: The same seeds in TypeScript, amounts assumed 6 decimals
steps: `create_escrow` derives the PDA from `["gifter_escrow", maker, BN(id).toArrayLike(Buffer, 'le', 8)]` and the vault as the ATA of mint A owned by that PDA, matching `create.rs`. Amounts are multiplied by `1e6`, so the app only makes sense for 6-decimal tokens (the script's mints were 6 decimals).

The escrow id is `Math.floor(Math.random() * 1000)` on submit, so two creates can collide (the program would then refuse the second with 'already in use'). The committed `PROGRAM_ID` is `9HP45DvS…`; the hosted build recorded on 13 Nov 2026 uses `45C1bSkF…`.

frontend.title: Accept calls take, Cancel calls refund, GFT is only a label
steps: `handleAccept` calls the client's `takeAndClose`. The 13 Nov 2026 click-through did not press Accept, because no escrow from another maker was left. `Cancel` is shown only when the connected wallet is the stored maker, and that click-through did refund.
The card says 'Accept to get GFT token reward!'. `REWARD_TOKEN_MINT` is used only for a navbar balance. The program has no mint instruction and never transfers GFT.

frontend.title: The token dropdown: the old query key, and this hosted build
steps: An earlier build put `walletAddress?.toBase58` — the function, not the call — in the react-query key, so the dropdown stayed empty. The hosted build recorded on 13 Nov 2026 uses the base58 string. That click-through listed 18 options, including mint A and mint B, and then created an escrow from the form (2c6QNtYz…).
Program transactions use the public devnet RPC. Only the DAS / enhanced-method calls in the hosted JS use a build-time URL.

exercises.title: Tell the failing take from the completed one
steps: Open the earlier failure (ck53TqoU…) and the 13 Nov 2026 take (33yMgZzA…) on Explorer.
Read [why this take failed](/articles/why-this-escrow-take-failed/) and name which program each signature belongs to.
exercises.expect: ck53TqoU… is `ProgramFailedToComplete` on `6Z5cvVUc…`, an access violation at `0x10008`. 33yMgZzA… completed on `45C1bSkF…`: 5 of mint B to the maker, 10 of mint A to the taker, vault and state closed. The hosted app is the second program.
exercises.hint: The hosted commit `fb2bbfd` has no `println!` in `send_to_maker`. The dangling `to_le_bytes().as_ref()` was in the seeds attribute of the earlier program.
exercises.approach: Use the two explorer links in the article. Do not look for `println!` in the hosted `take.rs`: it is not there. The article states which claims come from the pull request and which come from the devnet log.

exercises.title: Bind mint A, mint B and the maker to the stored escrow
steps: On `Take`, add `has_one = maker` (or `constraint = maker.key() == gifter_escrow_state.maker`) and `constraint = mint_a.key() == gifter_escrow_state.mint_a` and the same for `mint_b`.
A take that passes a different mint B should fail that constraint instead of paying an unexpected token.
exercises.expect: A take with the stored mints still completes, as 33yMgZzA… did. A take with a substituted mint B fails a constraint. We have not run that substituted case.
exercises.hint: The hosted `Take` accounts constrain `maker` to the stored key. They do not, in the excerpt, constrain `mint_a` or `mint_b` to the stored mints.
exercises.approach: Add `constraint = mint_a.key() == gifter_escrow_state.mint_a` and the same for mint B. The maker check is already in this commit. We have not run a substituted-mint take, so do not invent its error code.

exercises.title: Check the token dropdown against the 13 Nov record
steps: Connect a devnet wallet that holds the lesson's mints and open Create.
Count the options. The recorded click-through listed 18, including mint A and mint B, then created an escrow from the form.
exercises.expect: The dropdown is not empty on this hosted build. The recorded create from the form is 2c6QNtYz…. An earlier build stayed at 0 options because the query key stored `toBase58` without calling it.
exercises.hint: The deployment record says this build uses the base58 string as the query key and as `ownerAddress`.
exercises.approach: If the dropdown is empty, compare the hosted bundle with that record before changing the hook. The 13 Nov click-through already listed the tokens and submitted a create.

exercises.title: Add an expiry so a deposit cannot be locked forever
steps: Store a `deadline: i64` on `GifterEscrow`, set at create (Clock).
After the deadline, allow `refund` (and, if you like, a permissionless refund to the maker) even if the maker has disappeared. Before the deadline, take can still run.
exercises.expect: A past-deadline escrow can be unwound without take. An in-time refund should still work, as the 13 Nov script refund 3qwx8QBC… did. This program has no expiry field.
exercises.hint: There is no deadline on `GifterEscrow`. Until someone takes or the maker refunds, the deposit stays in the vault.
exercises.approach: Store a Clock deadline at create, and after it allow a refund to the maker. The 13 Nov refund 3qwx8QBC… is the in-time case already recorded. A past-deadline escrow was not run.

exercises.title: Stop promising a GFT reward the program does not mint
steps: Either remove the 'Accept to get GFT token reward!' copy and the navbar balance, or add a program instruction that mints or transfers a reward on a successful take (with a real mint authority and a recorded test).
exercises.expect: The card's promise matches what a successful take actually does. Today `REWARD_TOKEN_MINT` is only a navbar read; the program has no such instruction.
exercises.hint: The card says 'Accept to get GFT token reward!'. `REWARD_TOKEN_MINT` is only used for a navbar balance; the program has no mint instruction.
exercises.approach: Remove the promise, or add a real reward instruction and a recorded test. The card should then match what a successful take actually does.

It did not press Accept, because no escrow from another maker was left; the completed take is the script transaction 33yMgZzA…. The card still promises a GFT reward the program does not mint. The escrow list does not refresh until reload. Program 6Z5cvVUc… is still on devnet and its take aborted (ck53TqoU…); it is not the hosted app.
objectives: Create an escrow PDA and deposit mint A into an associated-token vault the PDA owns, naming mint B and a price.
Refund: the vault signs a transfer_checked back to the maker and both accounts close; an outsider cannot refund.
Tell a completed take (33yMgZzA… on 45C1bSkF…) from the earlier abort (ck53TqoU… on 6Z5cvVUc…).
prereqs: Phantom on devnet and a little devnet SOL. On the 13 Nov 2026 hosted build the token dropdown filled after connect.

[TrustLock](/lessons/trustlock/) immediately before this: you have just seen a SOL escrow with a Clock deadline. Here the vault is an SPL-token ATA, and there is no expiry. This is the last lesson in [stage 1](/lessons/path/#stage-1).

build.note: The Anchor workspace is `contract/` (`Cargo.toml` is Anchor 0.30.1). The fork's `declare_id!` is `9HP45DvS…`. The hosted program recorded on 13 Nov 2026 is `45C1bSkF…`. The build log below checked out an earlier commit, `a9c3a417…`, not the hosted commit `fb2bbfd`.
build.ran: On 13 Nov 2026 (Europe/London) we ran `git checkout a9c3a417d2d78294f58975b1461859ffb20df05a` and `/home/box/.avm/bin/anchor-0.30.1 build` in `contract/` with `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.89.0`. Cargo finished a release build in 1 m 13 s and wrote `target/deploy/gifter_escrow.so` (311,808 bytes, a valid ELF). Anchor then failed at 'Building IDL failed' with a `proc-macro-error` Span trait error — the same host-toolchain issue as DeVos, not a problem in this program. The default host rustc (1.99) is too new; use 1.89 (or another 1.8x). We did not run `anchor test`.
